data.hypothesis: Increasing each same-warp transpose subgroup from 8×8 to 16×16 reduces the lane/register-bit exchange count per 32×32 tile: two 16-lane groups per warp and two warps per tile require 128 shuffle operations versus 192 for the parent's four 8-lane groups per warp and four warps. It doubles values held per thread, so register pressure or occupancy may offset the fewer shuffles; only measurement can decide.

memory_lessons.applicability: A contrasting warp-shuffle tile-size experiment; the mechanism is not established by timing alone.
memory_lessons.claim: The correct 8×8 warp-shuffle parent measured 3.3350, 3.4902, and 3.4515 microseconds (mean 3.4256) for n=1024, versus the baseline mean of 16.9190 microseconds. This supports testing a different ownership granularity, but does not establish which mechanism caused the observed difference.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure the 16×16 subgroup variant for correctness and repeated n=1024 full-run times; inspect its ordinary build output for register count and spills.

data.notes: This candidate is not yet built or measured here, so there is no candidate register/spill report or repeated n=1024 timing evidence. The cited timings are the measured parent samples, not measurements of this variant. Each lane loads sixteen row values from its input column; lanes are split into two independent 16-lane column groups, and XOR exchanges remain within each same-warp group. The kernel uses no shared memory, block-wide barrier, or additional storage, and copies float bits through unsigned values.
transformations: Changed the warp mapping to use two warps per 32×32 tile, each processing a 16×32 input strip; each lane holds sixteen values loaded at adjacent input columns across rows.

Transposed each 16×16 lane/register subgroup with four stages of warp-local XOR shuffles using width 16; the two subgroups remain confined to the same warp and use no shared memory or CTA synchronization.
Stored each result with size_t matrix offsets and unsigned/float bitcasts to preserve exact float bit patterns; retained the run entry point and grid coverage for positive n divisible by 32.
